name: org.machanism.machai:project-layout
description: Project Layout is a Java utility library for detecting, describing, and working with conventional on-disk project directory layouts. It provides a common ProjectLayout abstraction for source roots, resource roots, test roots, documentation roots, modules, project identifiers, parent identifiers, and root-relative path operations. The library supports Maven projects through pom.xml metadata, Gradle projects through the Gradle Tooling API, JavaScript and TypeScript projects through package.json workspaces, Python projects through pyproject.toml, setup.py, setup.cfg, requirements.txt, Pipfile, and virtual environment indicators, and a fallback default filesystem-based layout. It is intended for build tooling, code generation, documentation tools, AI-assisted project processing, repository scanners, Maven and Gradle ecosystem integrations, and plugins that need reliable folder discovery across heterogeneous projects.

usageContext: Detect project type and layout from a filesystem directory
Locate source, resource, test, and documentation folders for Maven, Gradle, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and generic projects
Scan multi-module Maven, Gradle, and package.json workspace repositories
Build plugins and automation tools that need root-relative project paths
Prepare metadata for code processing, documentation generation, AI indexing, and repository traversal

constructors.description: Creates a Maven-specific project layout detector that reads pom.xml metadata to discover modules, production source and resource directories, test source and resource directories, documentation directories, project identifiers, project names, and parent identifiers.

examples.description: Instantiates the Maven layout detector, configures the project root directory, and reads root-relative source and test folders using Maven conventions and pom.xml metadata.

constructors.description: Creates a Gradle-specific project layout detector that uses the Gradle Tooling API to load a GradleProject model and expose child modules plus conventional Gradle source, test, and documentation roots.

examples.description: Creates a Gradle layout instance, assigns a Gradle project directory, and obtains module names and conventional documentation paths.

constructors.description: Creates a fallback project layout implementation that performs lightweight filesystem inspection and treats each immediate subdirectory of the configured project root as a potential module unless excluded.

examples.description: Uses the fallback layout to list immediate child directories as modules when no Maven, Gradle, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python metadata is available.

features.name: detectProjectLayout
features.signature: public static org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout detectProjectLayout(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.FileNotFoundException
features.description: Detects the appropriate ProjectLayout implementation for a directory by inspecting project metadata. The detector supports Maven projects, JavaScript or TypeScript package.json projects, Python projects, and a generic default layout fallback.

examples.description: Automatically detects the project layout type for a real repository and then uses the common ProjectLayout API to access source and test roots.

features.name: getSources
features.description: Returns root-relative production source and resource directories for a configured project layout. Implementations use ecosystem-specific metadata or conventions, such as Maven build source directories and resources or Gradle conventional src/main paths.

examples.description: Retrieves root-relative source directories and resolves them to absolute java.io.File instances for downstream scanning or processing.

features.name: getTests
features.description: Returns root-relative test source and test resource directories for the configured project layout. Maven implementations inspect build metadata and apply defaults; Gradle implementations expose conventional src/test roots.

examples.description: Detects the layout for a project and collects test directories for a test indexing, reporting, or quality analysis workflow.

features.name: getModules
features.description: Returns module directories or child module names for multi-module projects. MavenProjectLayout reads modules from pom.xml when packaging is pom, GradleProjectLayout reads child projects from the Gradle model, JScriptProjectLayout resolves package.json workspaces, and DefaultProjectLayout lists immediate subdirectories.

examples.description: Discovers modules in a repository and prints their identifiers for multi-module processing.

features.name: scanFolder
features.signature: public void scanFolder(java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Scans a project directory, detects its layout, processes modules when present, and delegates concrete handling to a subclass through processFolder(ProjectLayout). This is useful for implementing repository processors, documentation generators, indexers, and code analysis tools.

examples.description: Creates an anonymous ProjectProcessor that reports the detected layout type while scanFolder handles root and module traversal.

features.name: getRelativePath
features.signature: public static java.lang.String getRelativePath(java.io.File dir, java.io.File file, boolean addSingleDot)
features.description: Computes the path of a target file relative to a project directory and optionally prefixes it with ./ when appropriate. It returns null when the file is not located within the project directory.

examples.description: Converts an absolute or root-resolved file into a stable root-relative path suitable for metadata, logs, reports, or indexing.

customizations.name: ProjectProcessor.processFolder
customizations.description: Subclass ProjectProcessor and implement processFolder(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout) to define custom processing logic for a detected project or module layout.

examples.description: Defines a custom processor that can be invoked with scanFolder to process each detected project or module.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout
studs.description: Base abstraction for describing a project's conventional on-disk layout. Implementations translate build tool conventions and metadata into root-relative source, test, documentation, and module paths.

examples.description: Uses the abstract ProjectLayout API after automatic detection without depending directly on a concrete implementation.

examples.title: Install the library in a Maven project
steps: Add the dependency to the consumer project's pom.xml.
Use ProjectLayoutManager.detectProjectLayout(java.io.File) to detect a repository layout.
Call getSources(), getTests(), getDocuments(), or getModules() on the returned ProjectLayout.
examples.description: This scenario installs Project Layout as a Maven dependency, configures it only by passing the project root directory, and runs a practical layout detection workflow for a real repository.

examples.title: Build a repository scanner with ProjectProcessor
steps: Implement processFolder(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout) with the desired indexing, analysis, or reporting behavior.
Invoke scanFolder(java.io.File) with the repository root. The processor will detect modules and process each module or the root folder.
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to configure and run a custom project scanner that prints all detected source roots across a root project or its modules.

examples.title: Directly use MavenProjectLayout for a Maven-only tool
steps: Call projectDir(java.io.File) with the Maven project root containing pom.xml.
Run getModules(), getSources(), getTests(), and getDocuments() to drive a Maven-specific automation task.
examples.description: This practical Maven scenario bypasses automatic detection when the caller already knows the repository is Maven-based and wants source, documentation, and module metadata.
